title: The Service Sector Is Back In Favor
gist: A Gavekal teaser argues China is pivoting policy attention back toward services after years of Xi Jinping prioritizing manufacturing supremacy, driven by squeezed manufacturing margins and the AI boom. The body is truncated (paywall teaser, ~223 words) so only the setup thesis and historical framing are available.

insights.claim: Chinese officials from Xi Jinping down are now talking up services, spanning high-end research to low-end personal care, and issuing plans and targets to support the sector.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A top-down policy shift toward services signals coming stimulus, plans and targets that could favor consumer, healthcare, research and personal-services exposures over pure export manufacturers.
insights.quote: From Xi Jinping on down, Chinese officials are now talking up services, from high-end research to low-end personal care, and issuing plans and targets to support the sector.

insights.claim: This service focus is a notable reversal after Xi spent the past several years reorienting China's economy around an all-out pursuit of manufacturing supremacy.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Marks a potential inflection in China's growth model that investors positioned for the manufacturing/export theme should reassess.

insights.claim: Squeezed manufacturing margins and the AI boom have helped convince China's government it needs to correct the excesses of the previous manufacturing drive.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Thin manufacturing margins plus AI-fueled optimism are the stated catalysts; watch for margin compression in Chinese industrial exporters and AI-driven reallocation of capital.
insights.quote: The squeeze on manufacturing margins and the boom in artificial intelligence have helped convince the government that it needs to correct the excesses of the previous manufacturing drive.

insights.claim: Xi's focus on high technology as the key to national greatness has not wavered; only the execution of that strategy is adapting to current realities.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The tech-supremacy goal remains intact, so the services pivot is a tactical adjustment rather than abandonment of the tech agenda; long-term tech-policy bets stay in place.

insights.claim: Under Hu Jintao, Chinese government plans explicitly called for boosting the service sector's share of GDP and employment as a corrective to an industry-heavy economy inherited from the Maoist period.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Frames the current pivot as a return to a prior policy playbook, suggesting it could persist and mature into structural GDP-share targets rather than a one-off.
